title: Perfect derived objects are continuous under affine limits of qcqs spaces
statement: Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with schemes [def-pc-scheme], algebraic spaces and their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use quasi-coherent modules [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] and canonical tensor pullback [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. A space is quasi-compact if it admits a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme, and quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests. An affine morphism is representable and has affine source after pullback to any affine scheme test. Use the unbounded module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and K-flat derived tensor pullback with flat terms. An object is perfect if etale locally it is isomorphic in the derived category to a bounded complex of direct summands of finite free structure modules. Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed set, $(X_i,q_{ji})$ an inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic spaces with affine transitions $q_{ji}:X_j\to X_i$ for $j\ge i$, and $X=\varprojlim_iX_i$ with projections $q_i$. Derived pullback preserves perfect objects. Every perfect $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ is isomorphic to $Lq_i^*E_i$ for some $i$ and perfect $E_i\in D(\mathcal O_{X_i})$. For fixed perfect $E_i,F_i$, the canonical map $\operatorname{colim}_{j\ge i}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_{X_j})}(Lq_{ji}^*E_i,Lq_{ji}^*F_i)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_X)}(Lq_i^*E_i,Lq_i^*F_i)$ is a bijection. Here the Hom sets are taken in the derived categories, and iterated pullbacks use their canonical composition isomorphisms.

proof.text: First derived pullback preserves perfectness. On a local strict-perfect model, [lem-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-ringed-pullback-model] computes derived pullback by termwise pullback and preserves the finite-free retract splittings and degree bounds. Restriction to the pulled-back slice commutes with derived pullback by [lem-sbc-ringed-topos-sheaf-slice-derived-comparison]. The inverse images of the local covering form a covering, so these are local strict-perfect models for the pullback, as required by the definition.

For fixed perfect $E_i,F_i$, the latter has quasi-coherent cohomology by [lem-sfb-space-perfect-objects-compact]. Apply [lem-sfb-space-perfect-source-hom-continuity] with $P_i=E_i$ and $K_i=F_i$. This gives exactly the claimed bijection, with its canonical transition maps. We shall also use this bijection after replacing the base by any qcqs etale space over a fixed stage. In particular, a morphism at the limit descends; two stage morphisms with the same pullback become equal at a common later stage, by the equality relation defining a directed colimit of sets.

Fix a stage $i_0$. For a qcqs etale object $T_0\to X_{i_0}$, put $T_j=X_j\times_{X_{i_0}}T_0$ and $T=X\times_{X_{i_0}}T_0$. The base-change limit identity and affine projections are supplied by [lem-sfb-space-affine-limits-schematic-stages]. Use the property $P(T_0)$ that every perfect object on $T$ descends to a perfect object on some $T_j$, $j\ge i_0$. These spaces are qcqs: pull back a finite affine etale atlas of $T_0$ along the affine projection. The resulting atlas is still a finite union of affines, and its overlaps are affine over the original quasi-compact overlaps, hence quasi-compact. This verifies quasi-compactness and the diagonal criterion for quasi-separatedness. Thus Step 2 applies to these systems. We verify the affine case and distinguished-square implication required by [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-distinguished-square-induction]. The directed tail is small, nonempty and cofinal, so it does not change any limit or the descent assertion.

If $T_0$ is affine, all $T_j$ and $T$ are affine schemes, since their maps to $T_0$ are affine. Write $T_j=\operatorname{Spec}A_j$ and $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$; [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition] identifies $A=\operatorname{colim}_{j\ge i_0}A_j$. For perfect $E$ on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$, its quasi-coherent cohomology allows the equivalence [lem-sfb-derived-etale-zariski-equivalence] to write $E\simeq\epsilon_T^*E^{\mathrm{Zar}}$; [lem-sfb-etale-detects-perfect] makes $E^{\mathrm{Zar}}$ perfect. By [lem-pc-perfect-affine-bounded-projective] it is represented by $\widetilde{P^\bullet}$ for a bounded finite-projective $A$-complex. Apply [lem-pc-affine-perfect-colimit-descent] to obtain $P_j^\bullet\otimes_{A_j}A\cong P^\bullet$. Set $E_j=\epsilon_{T_j}^*\widetilde{P_j^\bullet}$. It is perfect by the affine criterion and etale detection. Finite projective terms are flat and the bounded model is K-flat; the affine pullback computation [lem-pc-affine-derived-pullback-tensor-tilde] and the pullback comparison of [lem-sfb-derived-etale-zariski-equivalence] give $L(T\to T_j)^*E_j\simeq E$. For the empty affine the same construction uses the zero complex.

For the induction implication, take an elementary distinguished square $(U_0\subset W_0,V_0\to W_0)$ with $U_0$ qc and $V_0$ affine, and suppose $P$ holds on $U_0,V_0,U_0\times_{W_0}V_0$. Let $E$ be perfect on $W=\lim W_j$. The properties on $U_0,V_0$ give, at a common stage $i$, perfect $A_i,B_i$ and isomorphisms $\alpha:LA_i\simeq E|_U$, $\beta:LB_i\simeq E|_V$. On $T=U\times_WV$ form $c_\infty=\beta^{-1}\alpha$. Step 2 on the qcqs overlap, whose limit is $T=\varprojlim_jT_j$ by [lem-sfb-space-affine-limits-schematic-stages], with the restrictions of $LA_i,LB_i$ to $T$ identified with the pullbacks of $A_i|_{T_i},B_i|_{T_i}$ by the comparison $\theta$ of [lem-sbc-ringed-topos-sheaf-slice-derived-comparison], descends $c_\infty$ and its inverse to some $T_j$. The two composites pull back to the identity; injectivity in the same directed Hom colimits makes both inverse equations hold after increasing $j$. Thus obtain an actual stage isomorphism $c_j:A_j|_{T_j}\simeq B_j|_{T_j}$ pulling back to $c_\infty$. Here $A_j,B_j$ are the derived pullbacks of the chosen models and remain perfect by Step 1.

Write $q:W\to W_j$ and $M=Rq_*E$. Adjunction $Lq^*\dashv Rq_*$ gives maps $a:A_j\to M|_{U_j}$ and $b:B_j\to M|_{V_j}$ adjoint to $\alpha$ and $\beta$. The restriction/direct-image comparisons and their mate identity in [lem-sbc-ringed-topos-sheaf-slice-derived-comparison] identify their restrictions to $T_j$ with the adjoints of $\alpha|_T$ and $\beta|_T$. Since $\beta|_T\circ Lc_j=\alpha|_T$, naturality of this adjunction yields $a|_{T_j}=b|_{T_j}\circ c_j$. The unbounded adjunction is the one specified in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]; no flatness of $q$ and no boundedness of $M$ is required. The base-changed square is elementary distinguished by [lem-sfb-space-distinguished-derived-gluing]. Apply its gluing assertion with target $M$ to obtain $E_j$, local isomorphisms to $A_j,B_j$, and $d:E_j\to Rq_*E$ restricting to $a,b$ under those isomorphisms.

The two maps $U_j\to W_j$ and $V_j\to W_j$ cover $W_j$: on the complement of $U_j$, the second is an isomorphism. Thus the local models $A_j,B_j$ show that $E_j$ is perfect. The adjoint $Lq^*E_j\to E$ of $d$ restricts to $\alpha$ and $\beta$, composed with the pulled-back gluing isomorphisms, by the mate identity in [lem-sbc-ringed-topos-sheaf-slice-derived-comparison]. It is therefore an isomorphism: its cone has cohomology sheaves restricting to zero on the etale cover $U,V$, so these sheaves are zero. This proves the distinguished-square implication. The affine case and [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-distinguished-square-induction] now give $P(X_{i_0})$. Taking $T_0=X_{i_0}$ descends every perfect object on $X$. Together with Steps 1 and 2 this proves all clauses.
